name: wifiphisher
summary: Fast automated phishing attacks against WPA networks.
highlights: -i — Manually choose an interface that supports both AP and monitor modes for spawning the rogu
-eI — Manually choose an interface that supports monitor mode for deauthenticating the victims.
-aI — Manually choose an interface that supports AP mode for spawning the rogue AP. Example: -aI
-iI — Choose an interface that is connected on the InternetExample: -iI ppp0
-mI — Choose an interface that is connected on the Internet in order to perform a MITM attack. A
-iAM — Specify the MAC address of the AP interface
-iEM — Specify the MAC address of the extensions interface
-iNM — Do not change any MAC address

flags.name: --help
flags.description: show this help message and exit

flags.name: --interface
flags.description: Manually choose an interface that supports both AP and monitor modes for spawning the rogue AP as well as mounting additional Wi-Fi attacks from Extensions (i.e. deauth). Example: -i wlan1

flags.name: --extensionsinterface
flags.description: Manually choose an interface that supports monitor mode for deauthenticating the victims. Example: -eI wlan1

flags.name: --apinterface
flags.description: Manually choose an interface that supports AP mode for spawning the rogue AP. Example: -aI wlan0

flags.name: --internetinterface
flags.description: Choose an interface that is connected on the InternetExample: -iI ppp0

flags.name: --mitminterface
flags.description: Choose an interface that is connected on the Internet in order to perform a MITM attack. All other interfaces will be protected.Example: -mI wlan1

flags.name: --mac-ap-interface
flags.description: Specify the MAC address of the AP interface

flags.name: --mac-extensions-interface
flags.description: Specify the MAC address of the extensions interface

flags.name: --no-mac-randomization
flags.description: Do not change any MAC address

flags.name: --keepnetworkmanager
flags.description: Do not kill NetworkManager

flags.name: --noextensions
flags.description: Do not load any extensions.

flags.name: --nodeauth
flags.description: Skip the deauthentication phase.

flags.name: --essid
flags.description: Enter the ESSID of the rogue Access Point. This option will skip Access Point selection phase. Example: --essid 'Free WiFi'

flags.name: --deauth-essid
flags.description: Deauth all the BSSIDs in the WLAN with that ESSID.

flags.name: --phishingscenario
flags.description: Choose the phishing scenario to run.This option will skip the scenario selection phase. Example: -p firmware_upgrade

flags.name: --presharedkey
flags.description: Add WPA/WPA2 protection on the rogue Access Point. Example: -pK s3cr3tp4ssw0rd

flags.name: --handshake-capture
flags.description: Capture of the WPA/WPA2 handshakes for verifying passphrase. Requires cowpatty. Example : -hC capture.pcap

flags.name: --quitonsuccess
flags.description: Stop the script after successfully retrieving one pair of credentials

flags.name: --lure10-capture
flags.description: Capture the BSSIDs of the APs that are discovered during AP selection phase. This option is part of Lure10 attack.

flags.name: --lure10-exploit
flags.description: Fool the Windows Location Service of nearby Windows users to believe it is within an area that was previously captured with --lure10-capture. Part of the Lure10 attack.

flags.name: --logging
flags.description: Log activity to file

flags.name: --disable-karma
flags.description: Disables KARMA attack

flags.name: --logpath
flags.description: Determine the full path of the logfile.

flags.name: --credential-log-path
flags.description: Determine the full path of the file that will store any captured credentials

flags.name: --payload-path
flags.description: Payload path for scenarios serving a payload

flags.name: --channel-monitor
flags.description: Monitor if target access point changes the channel.

flags.name: --wps-pbc
flags.description: Monitor if the button on a WPS-PBC Registrar is pressed.

flags.name: --wpspbc-assoc-interface
flags.description: The WLAN interface used for associating to the WPS AccessPoint.

flags.name: --known-beacons
flags.description: Broadcast a number of beacon frames advertising popular WLANs

flags.name: --force-hostapd
flags.description: Force the usage of hostapd installed in the system

flags.name: --phishing-pages-directory
flags.description: Search for phishing pages in this location

flags.name: --dnsmasq-conf
flags.description: Determine the full path of a custom dnmasq.conf file

flags.name: --phishing-essid
flags.description: Determine the ESSID you want to use for the phishing page
